newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks to end Colombia truckers' strike deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Talks to end Colombia truckers' strike deadlocked.

text.p: Talks to end a four-day-old strike by Colombian truck drivers were described as deadlocked by a union leader late on Wednesday, and he dismissed government threats to declare the work stoppage illegal as "meaningless."
Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), said negotiations with private transport companies and government officials continued on Wednesday night.

But he said "nothing significant" had come out of the talks so far, and stressed that opposition to the ACC's key demand -- for the government to set minimum cargo rates for overland freight -- did not bode well for the outcome.

Cargo rates are currently set on the basis of supply and demand, with no price guarantees for drivers, a practice that Suarez and other union officials say is driving rank-and-file members of the ACC, which represents about 80 percent of Colombian truckers, into bankruptcy.

Local media reports said the government had given the ACC a 24-hour ultimatum on Wednesday night to lift the strike that threatens to create serious problems with key of coffee, sugar, coal and other commodities.
But Suarez told Reuters "in practice this would have no effect," since nothing came of the government's decision to outlaw a previous strike in October.

Truckers affiliated with the ACC argue that there is no law requiring them, as private citizens, to provide any service to the state. Government officials say overland freight is essential, however, and that drivers could be ordered back to work in the interest of national security.

The latest strike, which industry sources say would disrupt coffee export schedules for May if it extends into next week, was called to protest against what Suarez and other union officials describe as the failure, by the government and private transport commpanies, to respect terms of an agreement ending the work stoppage that lasted 11 days last October.
